questions.questionText: Consider the logical statement: (A is greater than B) AND (B is greater than C). If both statements are TRUE, which of the following MUST also be true?
options: A and C must be equal
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: A is greater than C
questions.explanation: By the transitive property of inequality, if A > B and B > C, then A must strictly be greater than C.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Bebras International Challenge on Informatics and Computational Thinking.

questions.questionText: What is the next number in this sequence? 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, ___

questions.explanation: Each term is generated by multiplying the preceding number by 2 (geometric progression with ratio 2): 48 * 2 = 96.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Bebras International Challenge on Informatics and Computational Thinking.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following two operations:
x = 3
x = x + 2
What is the value stored in x after these lines execute?
options: I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.explanation: x initially holds 3. In the next line, the right side is evaluated (3 + 2 = 5) and reassigned back into x.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Code.org CS Principles: Variables and Sequencing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following real-life instructions describes an algorithmic LOOP (repeating an action until a condition is met)?
options: Stir the batter until no dry flour is visible, checking after every 10 stirs.
Turn on the oven and set temperature to 350 degrees.
If you have chocolate chips, add them; otherwise add nuts.
Pour the mixture into a round baking pan.
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Stir the batter until no dry flour is visible, checking after every 10 stirs.
questions.explanation: A loop repeats an action continuously until a terminating condition is fulfilled (no dry flour remaining).
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Code.org K-5 Computational Concepts: Loops and Repetition.

questions.explanation: You must first read the inputs before adding them, and compute the sum before dividing by 3.

questions.questionText: In a small beaver lodge network, Beaver A can talk to B, B can talk to C, and C can talk to D. If the communication channel between B and C collapses, can A still send a message to D?
options: No, because B and C was the only bridge connecting the two halves
Yes, messages reroute automatically through the air
No, Beaver A and B cannot talk anymore
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: No, because B and C was the only bridge connecting the two halves
questions.explanation: Removing bridge (B, C) partitions the connected graph into two disconnected components: {A, B} and {C, D}.
questions.source: Bebras International Challenge on Informatics and Computational Thinking
questions.attribution_text: Adapted under CC-BY-SA 4.0 from Bebras international task archives. Tasks inspire computational thinking without requiring prior programming syntax.

questions.questionText: A binary tree has 1 root node. The root has 2 child nodes, and each child node has 2 leaf nodes. How many total nodes are in this tree?
options: I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.explanation: Level 0 has 1 node, Level 1 has 2 nodes, Level 2 has 4 nodes. Total = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 nodes.
questions.source: Bebras International Challenge on Informatics and Computational Thinking
questions.attribution_text: Adapted under CC-BY-SA 4.0 from Bebras international task archives. Tasks inspire computational thinking without requiring prior programming syntax.

questions.questionText: A packet travels from Node S to Node T. Path 1 has delays [2ms, 5ms, 1ms]. Path 2 has delays [4ms, 3ms]. Path 3 has delays [3ms, 3ms, 3ms]. Which path delivers the packet with minimum total latency?
options: I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Path 2 (7ms total: 4 + 3)
questions.explanation: Path 1 sum = 8ms; Path 2 sum = 7ms; Path 3 sum = 9ms. Path 2 is the shortest path by total delay.
questions.source: Bebras International Challenge on Informatics and Computational Thinking
questions.attribution_text: Adapted under CC-BY-SA 4.0 from Bebras international task archives. Tasks inspire computational thinking without requiring prior programming syntax.

questions.questionText: Four students (W, X, Y, Z) must each be assigned to one of four unique project servers (1, 2, 3, 4). W can only use 1. X can use 1 or 2. Y can use 2 or 3. Z can use 3 or 4. Which server MUST be assigned to X?
options: I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Server 2
questions.explanation: Since W can only use Server 1, Server 1 is taken by W. X can use 1 or 2, but 1 is taken, so X must take Server 2. Subsequently Y takes 3, and Z takes 4.

questions.questionText: Task C depends on both Task A and Task B completing first. Task D depends on Task C completing first. Which of the following is a valid execution order for the four tasks?

questions.explanation: Both A and B must execute before C, and C must execute before D. B -> A -> C -> D satisfies all dependency constraints.

questions.questionText: A security door unlocks only if: (Card is Valid) AND ((PIN is Correct) OR (Biometric Matches)). If a student has a Valid Card, Incorrect PIN, and Matching Biometric, does the door unlock?

questions.questionText: What is the primary architectural purpose of a FOREIGN KEY in a relational schema?

questions.questionText: Table Students has 10 rows. Table Enrollments has 15 rows. If an INNER JOIN is performed ON Students.id = Enrollments.student_id and 3 students have no enrollments, what rows are returned?

All 10 student rows filled with NULLs
All 15 enrollment rows plus 3 empty rows

questions.questionText: When would a developer choose a LEFT OUTER JOIN instead of an INNER JOIN?

When sorting results in descending order

questions.questionText: What is the key functional difference between WHERE and HAVING in an aggregated query?

WHERE is only used with numbers; HAVING is used with text

questions.questionText:

MAX(salary) is invalid inside GROUP BY

questions.questionText: How does adding a B-Tree index on a frequently searched column improve query performance?

It compresses table size on disk by 50%

It turns the database into a distributed key-value cache

questions.attribution_text: Authored by CSE PathFinder Curriculum Team grounded in ANSI SQL standards.

questions.questionText: What does the 'I' in the database ACID transaction properties stand for?

questions.questionText: What is the role of the OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) clause in a window function?

questions.questionText: A table is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and what additional condition is satisfied?

questions.questionText: Guided Activity (Code.org Data Science Lab): You are analyzing a smart campus sensor dataset to determine which lecture halls waste the most electricity on weekends. What initial exploratory step should you perform first?
options: Filter the dataset for Saturday and Sunday timestamps, then calculate mean kilowatt-hours per room
Immediately delete all sensor readings below 10 degrees Celsius
Manually rewrite every sensor reading into a paper notebook
Format all room names in all-caps text without inspecting any energy numbers
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Filter the dataset for Saturday and Sunday timestamps, then calculate mean kilowatt-hours per room
questions.explanation: Effective data exploration begins by isolating the relevant target timeframe (weekends) and aggregating energy metrics by entity (room) to uncover outliers and patterns.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Code.org CS Principles Unit 9 Data Exploration curriculum under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

questions.questionText: Guided Activity (Code.org App Lab): You are building a mobile task manager. When a student taps 'Mark Done', the button should turn green and the completed count must increase by 1. In event-driven UI design, how is this handled?
options: Attach an 'onEvent' click handler to the button that increments the state variable and updates the button styling property
Run an infinite while-loop that continuously checks if the screen is being touched
Restart the entire operating system on every button click
Send an email to the server before showing any visual feedback to the user
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Attach an 'onEvent' click handler to the button that increments the state variable and updates the button styling property
questions.explanation: Modern interactive web and mobile apps rely on asynchronous event listeners ('onEvent' / 'addEventListener') that update application state and DOM properties reactively without freezing the UI.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Code.org App Lab Event-Driven Programming under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

questions.questionText: Guided Activity (Code.org Cybersecurity & Internet Lab): You are transmitting sensitive medical records across a public Wi-Fi network. Which security measure ensures that eavesdroppers on the router cannot read the payload?
options: Encrypting the payload end-to-end using TLS / HTTPS cryptographic certificates
Renaming the file extension from .pdf to .txt before sending
Turning your laptop screen brightness to zero during transmission
Sending the transmission in three separate emails at the same minute
I don't know / haven't learned this yet
questions.answer: Encrypting the payload end-to-end using TLS / HTTPS cryptographic certificates
questions.explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS/HTTPS) encrypts communication across untrusted networks so intermediaries intercepting packets only see cryptographically scrambled ciphertext.
questions.attribution_text: Adapted from Code.org CS Principles Unit 10 Cybersecurity and the Internet under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

questions.questionText: Guided Career Activity (Debugging & Testing Lab): A banking calculation function intermittently returns negative balances for active accounts. As a QA / Junior Software Engineer, what is the most professional debugging workflow?

questions.answer: Write a minimal reproducible unit test with the exact edge-case input and step through the calculation with a debugger

questions.attribution_text: Original hands-on software engineering laboratory exercise authored by CSE PathFinder Curriculum Team.

questions.questionText: Guided Career Activity (Cloud & API Engineering Lab): You are designing a REST API endpoint where users create a new project. Which HTTP method and HTTP status code pair should be returned upon successful creation?

questions.attribution_text: Original hands-on software engineering laboratory exercise authored by CSE PathFinder Curriculum Team.
